sentences.span: a big chunk of Monday's rally was dealers being forced to buy
sentences.why: McElligott's note frames Monday's advance as mechanical dealer hedging flow (the 'Vanna Machine' / vol-crush forced buying), not organic conviction buying; the pulse's thesis sentence restates that stance faithfully as a lead-in before naming the bank in s3.

sentences.span: Thursday ended up as the biggest put day in CBOE history. Dealers who sold all those puts hedged by shorting futures... Dealers had to buy back a BRICK of Short $Delta / Futures
sentences.why: Matches the mechanism exactly: dealers short puts (having sold them) hedged with short futures, then as spot rose and vol collapsed those puts lost delta, forcing dealers to buy back the futures hedge.

sentences.span: the Nomura cross-asset guru says the breadth was the sideshow
sentences.why: Directly supported: McElligott explicitly calls the 84%-advancing breadth the 'sideshow' and the vol crush the 'far and away standout' story.

sentences.span: the same strategist now writes that "the capitulation process is far along"... keeps his S&P 500 target at 8,000
sentences.why: 'Far along' and the 8,000 target are both verbatim. The 'year-end' qualifier is confirmed in the companion JPM morning briefings (25883/26229/26491), which label it explicitly: "Dubravko reiterates his YE26 SPX price target of 8,000 with $365 EPS, 21.9x."

sentences.span: a marginal new low... somewhere between 7,100 and 7,300... This would serve as a classic "re-test" that marks the end of the correction
sentences.why: Exact match on both the range and the 'retest to finish' framing.
